analysis:
Examined GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift (base and head) and the ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift patch and base. No concrete security regression identified.

GLM5NextPromptPolicy changes: (1) The raw-control capture now also decodes assistant `reasoning` and `reasoning_details` text from `messages` (head lines 110-113, 251-277). It uses `try?`, so failures are silent, and only `reasoning.text` details are used. The text is attached as `reasoning_content` only for assistant messages with none set (head 360-362), and only when the capture count aligns with the prepared messages (head 397-406). This is the requester's own history rendered into its own prompt. It is not cross-tenant and adds no logging or telemetry. Possible concern: request-controlled text enters the template. That is the same trust class as message content, and it is bound by the template. Delimiter checks apply to tool-call arguments, not to reasoning text, which the official template presumably handles; this is not shown to be a regression.
(2) The null-tolerant `present()` helper, `thinking` object handling and summary levels loosen parsing. Unknown keys still set `invalid`. Contradictory switches are still refused in `validate()`. Exclusion refusal is preserved. Note that `preserve_thinking` alone is now the only top-level invalid key, because `thinking` is parsed separately. A failed decode inside `thinking` is caught and sets `invalid` (head 231-233).
(3) The `strict` tool rejection was removed (head 347-350). The comment says every auto call is schema-validated via ToolConstraintValidation.validate. That validation lives outside the supplied evidence, so I could not verify it. Required or named tool_choice is still rejected (head 326-328). This is a prompt-contract and quality matter, not a threat-model asset breach.
(4) An empty tool-call arguments string now yields `[:]` (head 443), a benign relaxation.

ErrorMapping: a new `.unsupportedOutputControl` case maps to clientError, invalidRequest and 400. This is consistent with the other client-fault cases and keeps sanitized bounded failures. The enum definition is not in the supplied batch, and the switches are exhaustive, so a compile-time mismatch would surface elsewhere.

Remaining integration questions: where `.unsupportedOutputControl` is thrown, and whether strict-schema validation truly covers all tool calls. Neither affects the prefix-cache T-041 scope directly. The reasoning text does enter prompts and therefore prefix-cache keys, but it is still scoped by coordinator cacheSalt.
